description.p: A Google Takeout export keeps the capture date of each photograph in a small JSON file beside the image rather than inside it. Copy the photos into a gallery and that file stays behind, so a lifetime of pictures appears to have been taken on the day the export was downloaded.
Nostos writes that information back where every photo manager looks for it, working entirely on your own machine.

ul.li: Writes capture date, coordinates, description, recognised faces and the favourite mark into the EXIF tags, without recompressing the image
Derives the real local time from the coordinates, daylight saving included, instead of writing universal time and shifting every photograph by a time zone
Merges an export that was split across several archives, and reports a missing piece from an interrupted download
Records which photographs belonged to which album before any deduplication, because an album is exported as a second copy of the file and nothing else
Finds duplicates by content rather than by name, so two files that share a name and a size but differ inside both survive
Exports deduplicated vCard contacts and iCalendar calendars, with proprietary fields removed
Checks free disk space before any operation that copies, and offers a way forward when a library will not fit twice

description.p: No function in this application deletes a file. The default is to write repaired copies into a separate folder and leave the originals untouched; where files are moved, a ledger is written beside them and one button puts everything back.

The application opens no network connections at all. There is no account, no telemetry, no crash reporting and no automatic updater. That is not a statement of intent: the build fails if a networking library enters the dependency graph, and the check runs on every change.

description.p: Adds a version panel that states how old the installed copy is, worked out from the compile date and the local clock rather than by asking a server. Formatting and the last untranslated strings fixed.
